statement: A native Raft group that accepts an exact, durable-identity inbound envelope as CORE_OK/inbound-enqueued must own the bounded scheduled drain as admitted work, even when no unrelated event-loop handle remains. Every admitted envelope either reaches the real lifecycle-admitted core/Ready/application/publication path, or stays as explicitly owned and typed deferred debt; it cannot disappear on idle-process exit. Close and replacement retire its exact scheduling resources without leaving referenced background work.

constraints.statement: This is a separate bounded runtime scheduling/lifetime repair. The existing seed-participant-release-applied-position-barrier Quest remains open and does not authorize scheduling changes. Change only the canonical native runtime/operation-port timer-lifecycle interaction and owned tests. Do not alter release OBSERVE, PA/R/K assessment, application commit, transport ACK, Raft queue semantics or membership.

An acknowledged queued inbound message is admitted work and cannot rely on an unrelated socket, polling reader or observer timeout to keep its one scheduled turn alive. Idle background election/diagnostic timers do not gain process liveness. Do not add a second execution driver, a new timer, a caller-local tick or a read side effect.

Use existing inbound drain scheduler and existing persistence-admission retry bound. Preserve one pending timer and its original timeSource/handle, deterministic cleanup on close/replacement, no expired timer resurrection, no stale owner entry. Do not increase existing retry budgets, ratchets or deadlines; a healthy exhausted bound remains red.

V13 two exact original step results are CORE_OK/inbound-enqueued, yet both progress callbacks remain absent and a Node beforeExit listener emits a bounded record. V14 uses the original core-entry seam to observe zero whole-group core entries after both accepted handoffs. Those are diagnostics, not proof of which private timer branch executed. First add identity-correct passive scheduling/entry/retirement evidence without reads, refs, timers or changing the original promises. Never attribute group-only counters to a replica.

Prove an engaged, named failure from the unchanged-runtime source, not mere unresolved Promise, missing symbol, timeout or setup. Prove uninstrumented native N-to-K candidate success with identical controls on the same physical host as an unchanged-source negative. Native diagnostic runs on hosted CI can qualify stage attribution but never replace a locked-host positive.

Independently review exact source and all affected timer, operation-port and shutdown categories before landing. Preserve clean source-only negative, current-identity custody and complete artifact hashes. Refresh canonical test impact metadata, then validate genuine fresh-seed, FreshMG, TX1/TX2, CDC, snapshot, zero-legacy and off-seed recovery on final composition. This Quest alone does not merge or publish main.
